children: , the memory-chip and data-storage giant, jumped approximately 1.2% to $942.77 before Tuesday's opening bell. Investors shrugged off a potential strike in Taiwan, Micron's most important manufacturing base. Two unions representing nearly 10,000 workers in Taoyuan and Taichung want a bigger share of the company's record profits.

The message from workers is loud. More than 80% of surveyed union members backed possible industrial action. Their demands include a one-time payment and quarterly bonuses equal to 15% of operating profit starting in fiscal 2027. Micron says this year's performance bonus will already be its largest ever, but the two sides are still talking.

The timing could not be sharper. Micron's latest quarter delivered $41.46 billion in revenue, $28.24 billion in net income and $18.3 billion in adjusted free cash flow. Yet the stock now trades 53.67% above its $613.51 GF Value. That premium signals huge confidenceand almost no patience for a factory shutdown.

title: Micron Rises Despite Potential Strike, Trades 53.67% Above GF Value
